# 202 — explainer: the arrival tag analytics was dropping

Written before merge, per the risk policy. Full walkthrough + quiz because the changed-line
total (48 changed + 231 new test lines ≈ 279) exceeds the 150-line LOW cap under item 198's
counting precedent, even though every other LOW indicator holds — the verifier assigns the
tier independently.

## Goal

Make the product's own acquisition tag, `src`, arrive in Mixpanel on every event instead of
on none.

## The intuition, in one picture

The site hands out three kinds of tagged links, all of them ours:

| link | tag it carries | who makes it |
|---|---|---|
| `/plan.html?waitlist=1&src=seo_token` — on all 2,180 static SEO pages (×2 with KO) | `seo_token` / `seo_chain` | items 062 / 066 / 075 |
| the spotlight pack links the human posts to X | `x_spotlight` | items 064 / 069 |
| **"Garden this pool →"**, the north-star CTA | `pool` | item 143 |

`analytics.js` reads the landing URL once, at `init()`, and keeps whatever attribution params
it finds for the whole session — that object is spread onto *every* event by
`getBaseContext()`. It was reading `utm_source`, `utm_medium`, `utm_campaign`, `utm_term`,
`utm_content`, `ref`, `gclid`, `fbclid`, `twclid`. Nine params, every one of them a
*third-party* tag. The one tag **we** put on **our own** links was not on the list.

So the only way `src` ever reached Mixpanel was `planner.js:4029` reading it by hand and
passing it as `source` to the five `waitlist_*` emitters. Everything else — `page_view`,
`session_start`, `pool_view`, `pool_click` (the north star), `plan_created`, `plan_saved`,
`share_link_created` — arrived anonymous.

## Why it mattered enough to build

The daily heartbeat has been reporting, for twenty consecutive days:

> `page_view` by `src` → one row, `undefined` = 47. **Zero tagged arrivals.**

That reads like a finding about distribution. It is not: `page_view` has no `src` property to
break down, so a spotlight click, an SEO-page waitlist click and a cold direct hit are
indistinguishable **by construction**. A real tagged arrival would have shown up as
`undefined` too. This is the "a detector that cannot see" failure mode the loop has now fixed
five times on its own audit tooling (166, 198, 199, 200, 201) — this instance was on the
*product's* analytics, sitting on the north-star funnel.

## What changed, in reading order

**1. `analytics.js` — the whole product change (one line + a comment).**

```js
['utm_source', 'utm_medium', 'utm_campaign', 'utm_term', 'utm_content',
-  'ref', 'gclid', 'fbclid', 'twclid'].forEach((k) => {
+  'ref', 'gclid', 'fbclid', 'twclid', 'src'].forEach((k) => {
   const v = params.get(k);
   if (v) out[k] = String(v).substring(0, 200); // cap length (privacy/safety)
 });
```

`src` gets exactly `ref`'s treatment: 200-char cap, key omitted entirely when the param is
absent (never the string `"undefined"`), inside the existing `try`/`catch`. The comment above
it records *why* an internal tag sits beside third-party click ids.

Nothing else in any product file. `planner.js`'s `source` threading is byte-identical — the
two are different properties with different meanings and must not be merged: on `pool_click`,
`source` means *which CTA was clicked* (`garden_cta` / `protocol_link`, NORTH_STAR line 29),
while `src` means *how the visitor arrived*. Collapsing them would break the north-star query.

**2. `test_analytics_acquisition.js` — extended (+34/−6).** The pure-Node rig from item 064.
Asserts `src` is captured, is capped at 200 chars, is absent as a key when the param is
absent, and is spread onto an emitted event by `getBaseContext()` (asserted through the event
props, not by reading the source array).

**3. `test_analytics_src_attribution.js` — new (231 lines), real Chromium.** Fixtures and
mixpanel-stub pattern lifted from `test_waitlist_seo_entry.js`, port 8869. Five cases:

- `/plan.html?waitlist=1&src=seo_token` (the literal URL every static token page links to) →
  a track call carries `src === 'seo_token'`, **and** `waitlist_opened.source` is still
  `'seo_token'` — the non-regression half.
- `/?pool=<real snapshot pool id>&src=seo_token` → `pool_view` carries `src === 'seo_token'`.
  This is the north-star surface, and it is why leg 2 (below) becomes a pure generator change.
- Both URLs **without** `?src=` → no `src` key anywhere. Controls, so the assertions can't
  pass by accident.
- No unexpected page errors across any case.

**4. `package.json` — `test:serial` gains the new file** immediately after
`test_analytics_acquisition.js`. (`run-tests.js` auto-discovers; `test:serial` is
hand-maintained, so it needed the edit — grepped, not assumed.)

## Non-vacuity

Deleting `'src'` from the list turned **5 assertions red by name** (3 unit, 2 rendered) and
left every other assertion — including both controls and the `waitlist_opened.source`
non-regression half — green. `analytics.js` was restored byte-identically:
`md5 3966e6e5a9608c7079ca93958b564d6d` before the probe and after the restore. Full transcript
in `202-notes.md`.

## Deviations from the spec

One, disclosed in `202-notes.md`: the build agent's brief scoped bookkeeping
(`BACKLOG.md`, `LOG.md`, this file) to the operator, so the agent left criterion 9 to this
commit rather than doing it itself. It lands in the same commit either way, which is what the
2026-07-13 rule actually requires.

## What this does NOT ship — stated plainly

**A measurement fix, not a traffic fix.** Tagged arrivals will very likely still read zero
tomorrow: there is little traffic, and the static estate's eight `?pool=` deep links per page
carry no tag at all yet. That second leg — threading `src=seo_token` / `src=seo_chain` through
`generate-token-pages.js:589-591`'s shared `poolHrefFor()` — was deliberately **not built**
here: it regenerates ~4,360 HTML files and is HIGH-tier SEO surface deserving its own diff.
Its exact anchors are filed in `202-notes.md` for the next item.

What ships is that the property becomes *populatable*, and that a twenty-day-old line in the
daily report stops being a vacuous signal.
